boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UC Santa Cruz rituals and recurring celebrations, from slug lore to campus community gatherings.

cards.title: Rally behind a banana slug
cards.subtitle: UC Santa Cruz campus identity
cards.notes: Spot Sammy at a campus event or game, then use the full “Banana Slug” name when sharing the mascot’s distinctive campus story.
cards.short_summary: Students’ 1986 choice of a banana slug remains the university’s official mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Santa Cruz states that students voted in 1986 to adopt the Banana Slug as the official campus mascot.
cards.access_notes: A campus identity tradition; Sammy appears at sports events and other university functions.

cards.title: Say “Fiat Slug!”
cards.subtitle: A rallying cry from the mascot fight
cards.notes: Use the phrase as a piece of UCSC history, and pair it with the story of students organizing to keep the Banana Slug over the Sea Lion.
cards.short_summary: “Fiat Slug,” meaning “Let there be Slug,” became part of the campaign for the Banana Slug.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Santa Cruz documents Fiat Slug as a student-era rallying phrase and logo connected to the successful Banana Slug campaign.
cards.source_title: As the slug rises: Once subversive, UCSC’s beloved mascot turns 25
cards.access_notes: A historical campus expression, not an instruction for participation in any restricted activity.

cards.title: Cheer “Slime ’em!”
cards.subtitle: Banana Slug athletics folklore
cards.notes: If you attend a Slug game, recognize this documented cheer as part of the student push that kept the campus mascot proudly unconventional.
cards.short_summary: Students used “Slime ’em!” and “Go Slugs!” while advocating for the Banana Slug.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Santa Cruz’s mascot history reports that students at basketball games yelled “Slime ’em!” and “Go slugs!” during the 1980s mascot dispute.
cards.source_title: As the slug rises: Once subversive, UCSC’s beloved mascot turns 25
cards.access_notes: Cheering is appropriate at publicly accessible athletics events; follow event-entry rules.

cards.title: March into Kresge Presents PRIDE
cards.subtitle: Annual march and festival at Porter Quad
cards.notes: Join the student-led march and festival when scheduled; look for campus resource tables, performances, and community-centered programming at Porter Quad.
cards.short_summary: Kresge’s annual Pride march and festival has recognized queer identity and community since 2007.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Santa Cruz identifies Kresge Presents PRIDE as an annual student-led march and festival begun by the Kresge College Programs Office in 2007.
cards.source_title: Kresge Presents PRIDE: 17th annual celebration of queer identity and community
cards.access_notes: Check Kresge College programming for the current date, route, and festival details.

cards.title: Celebrate graduating Chicane and Latiné Slugs
cards.subtitle: El Centro’s annual year-end ceremony
cards.notes: Attend or support this bilingual graduation-season gathering, which combines recognition of graduates with cultural performances and community celebration.
cards.short_summary: El Centro’s year-end celebration honors Chicane and Latiné graduates, their resilience, and cultural pride.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Santa Cruz calls the Chicane Latiné Year-End Celebration a beloved annual campus tradition hosted by El Centro.
cards.source_title: Intergenerational keynote speakers Becky G and Olga Talamante inspire graduates at UC Santa Cruz Chicane Latiné Year-End Celebration
cards.access_notes: Held during commencement season; confirm the current program and guest guidance with El Centro.

cards.title: Gather for the Powwow
cards.subtitle: American Indian Resource Center community celebration
cards.notes: Follow the American Indian Resource Center’s guidance when the Powwow returns, and engage respectfully with dance, song, vendors, and intertribal performances.
cards.short_summary: The Powwow reconnects UC Santa Cruz with local Native communities through cultural gathering and performance.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Santa Cruz describes its Powwow as a celebration organized by the American Indian Resource Center, SANAI, and Cabrillo College.
cards.access_notes: Programming and venue can change; use American Indian Resource Center announcements for current details.

cards.title: Bring family into the redwoods
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide fall family gathering
cards.notes: Invite your support network to the scheduled fall weekend for workshops, meet-and-greets, and a firsthand look at campus academic and community life.
cards.short_summary: Launched in fall 2024, Family Weekend is a new campus-wide tradition for students and their families.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Santa Cruz says its inaugural campus-wide Family Weekend began a new tradition rooted in connection, belonging, and student success.
cards.access_notes: Use the Slug Family Hub or university announcements for the current schedule and registration information.

cards.title: Return to the Redwoods with alumni
cards.subtitle: Annual alumni campus weekend
cards.notes: If you are an alum or graduating student, watch Alumni Network announcements for the weekend’s campus experiences and opportunities to reconnect.
cards.short_summary: Return to the Redwoods is an annualizing alumni weekend built around reconnecting with UC Santa Cruz.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Santa Cruz reported that Return to the Redwoods had its second annual gathering in 2024 and that alumni planned to continue it annually.
cards.source_title: Return to the Redwoods 2024: Reconnecting with UCSC and each other
cards.access_notes: This is an alumni-oriented event; check the Alumni Network for eligibility and current dates.

cards.title: Listen at the Morton Marcus Poetry Reading
cards.subtitle: Annual Humanities Institute poetry event
cards.notes: Check the Humanities Institute calendar for the next November reading, then arrive ready to hear a visiting poet in the campus’s long-running public series.
cards.short_summary: The annual reading continues a Santa Cruz poetry tradition while bringing acclaimed poets to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The UC Santa Cruz Humanities Institute states that the annual Morton Marcus Poetry Reading continues Morton Marcus’s 40-year tradition of bringing acclaimed poets to Santa Cruz County.
cards.access_notes: The Humanities Institute says the reading is held each November; verify the current venue and program before attending.

cards.title: Dance at the annual Dizikes Concert
cards.subtitle: Cowell College alumni-weekend tradition
cards.notes: Look for the concert during alumni weekend and enjoy the program in the Cowell Provost’s House yard, honoring professor emeritus John Dizikes.
cards.short_summary: The Dizikes Concert is a recurring Alumni Weekend gathering honoring John Dizikes.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Santa Cruz describes the annual Dizikes Concert as a cherished tradition of its Alumni Weekend celebrations.
cards.access_notes: Check Alumni Weekend and Cowell College announcements for the current concert schedule and attendance details.
